source.title: Effective Quantization of Muon Optimizer States
source.authors: Aman Gupta; Rafael Celente; Abhishek Shivanna; D. T. Braithwaite; Gregory Dexter; Shao Tang; Hiroto Udagawa; Daniel Silva; R. Ramanath; S. Keerthi

record.file_problem: The text appears to contain the full paper and appendix; no relevant truncation or garbling noted.
record.tranche_reason: The study sweeps GPT model sizes and reports held-out pretraining loss and downstream benchmark averages, but does not fit or test the scaling-law equations or compute-optimal allocation claimed in the original sources.
record.gate_note: The paper reports a parameter-size sweep with validation losses, so those measurements bear on V1, and reports downstream benchmark averages across sizes, bearing on V6. It uses the cited compute-optimal guidance to set approximately 20 training tokens per parameter; it does not vary the parameter/token split at a fixed compute budget. Quantization comparisons, SFT results, and ImageNet results do not test the specified scaling-law versions. Results cited from other work are not included as rows.
record.test_reason: The study adopts Hoffmann et al.'s approximately 20 tokens per parameter to evaluate optimizer quantization. Its size sweep measures whether quantized Muon preserves baseline quality; it does not evaluate power-law form, extrapolation, compute-optimal allocation, or downstream prediction. Reporting improving loss and benchmark averages across sizes does not by itself test those relationships.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that linear 8-bit quantization of Muon's state can preserve full-precision quality while reducing optimizer-state memory by about 62% at 2.7B parameters. Quantizing the remaining AdamW states increases savings to about 75% with small quality degradation. They do not conclude that a scaling-law version has been established or qualified.
record.recipe_differences: This is an optimizer-quantization study, not a replication of scaling-law fits. It uses approximately 20 training tokens per parameter and does not fit loss curves or sweep compute-optimal parameter/token allocations.
record.method_sensitivity: Model size and optimizer/quantization variant differ across reported outcomes; training tokens increase with model size at approximately 20 tokens per parameter.

fits_no_version.finding: Validation losses decline across five model sizes, while Muon-8L/AdamW-32 remains within 0.002 of Muon-32. Fully quantizing the AdamW component causes small additional losses.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Quantizing Muon's optimizer state preserves pretraining quality across the tested model sizes.

fits_no_version.finding: Six-task averages increase across sizes for all three optimizers, and quantizing Muon alone largely preserves baseline downstream performance.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Muon optimizer-state quantization preserves downstream benchmark quality across the tested sizes.

record.problems: The parameter sweep covers only 162M to 2.7B and increases training tokens with parameter count; no scaling-law fit, exponent, independent token/compute sweep, or extrapolation is reported. The downstream aggregate averages have no uncertainty reported in the table.
record.rows_left_out: No otherwise eligible findings left out. The paper's optimizer quantization and memory comparisons, SFT comparisons, and ImageNet optimizer results do not measure the scaling-law outcomes in the claim versions.

untested.parts: Power-law form over several orders of magnitude with other resources non-bottlenecked; the five-size sweep jointly increases parameters and tokens.
Prediction of substantially larger runs from small-run fits.
Loss-minimising parameter/token allocations at fixed compute and their scaling exponents; the allocation is adopted rather than tested.
Architecture comparisons at fixed parameter count.
Power-law form in other modalities or training regimes; SFT and ImageNet experiments compare optimizers.
Predictive relationships between downstream performance and scale or pretraining loss; benchmark averages are reported to assess optimizer quality parity.
Dependence of scaling exponents or optimal allocation on setup and fitting choices, and departures from a single power law.

record.verdict_notes: The extracted table values are accurate. The original limits_scope labels mistake untested properties for demonstrated limitations. These optimizer comparisons should not be treated as scaling-law result rows.

versions.untested_parts: No power-law fit or exponent is reported; parameters, tokens and compute are not varied independently; the sweep spans 162M to 2.7B parameters, with training tokens increasing at approximately 20 tokens per parameter.
No extrapolation from small runs to larger runs is evaluated.
No fixed-compute comparison of parameter/token allocations or fitted compute-optimal trends is performed.
No controlled comparison of architectures at a fixed parameter count is reported.
The paper reports optimizer quantization experiments in pretraining, SFT, and ImageNet training, but does not test whether power-law forms hold across those regimes or modalities.
Downstream benchmark averages are reported across model sizes, but there is no predictive fit, extrapolation, or analysis relating downstream performance to pretraining loss.
The paper does not compare scaling-law fitting choices or report bending away from a fitted power law.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: GPT size sweep from 162M to 2.7B parameters, with training tokens increasing at approximately 20 per parameter
reader_labels.reason: The reported losses decline with size, but the study does not establish a power-law form, isolate parameter effects from tokens and compute, or cover several orders of magnitude; see r1–r15.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Six-task average across the five GPT sizes and three optimizer variants
reader_labels.reason: The reported aggregate scores rise overall with size, but the paper does not fit a predictive relationship or test prediction from pretraining loss; see r16–r30.
